chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The waiting period and the menstruation are for the women; when they claim, they are ratified.

key_terms.الْعِدَّةُ: The waiting period (iddah) a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband before remarrying
key_terms.صُدِّقَتْ: She is believed/ratified (her testimony is accepted as true)

ai.seo_question: Are women's claims about their menstruation and waiting period accepted in Shia law?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of 'tasdiq al-nisa' (believing the woman) in matters of personal status, specifically regarding the determination of the waiting period (iddah) and menstruation. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational rule of evidence where a woman's unilateral claim is accepted as valid proof unless contradicted by clear evidence, reflecting the legal presumption of truth in private matters. This principle underscores the reliability of female testimony in contexts where direct male observation is often impossible.
